summary: Hajime Sakurabe was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Otani University under Issai Funahashi and Susumu Yamaguchi, completing his PhD in 1967. He served at Otani University (1949–1986, becoming professor in 1971) and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (~1957–1959).

Hajime Tanabe was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Raphael von Koeber, Kyoto University, Berlin, and Freiburg under Martin Heidegger and Heinrich Rickert. He held posts at Tohoku University (1913) and Kyoto University (1919–1945).
Hakuin Ekaku was an active figure in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under Dōkyō Etan (~1708) and Hakuyūshi (~1710–1711), and later taught Suiō Genro.

Hakuju Ui was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu, and later in Tübingen, Oxford, and Cambridge. He held teaching posts at Tokyo, Tohoku, Komazawa (president, 1941), and Nagoya.

Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Bokusan Nishiari, Daiun Sogaku Harada, and Genpo Tsuyama, and graduated from Toshima Normal School in 1914. In 1954, he founded Sanbo Zen.

Hakuyu Hadano was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held posts at Tohoku University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1953–1959) and later became professor emeritus.

Hakuyu Taizan Maezumi was a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied at Komazawa University, Soji-ji, and San Francisco State University, under Hakujun Kuroda, Koryu Osaka, and Hakuun Ryoko Yasutani. He served as priest at Zenshuji Soto Mission in 1956.

Halle O'Neal specializes in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Kansas under Sherry Fowler and serves as Co-Director at the University of Edinburgh.

Hammalawa Saddhatissa worked in Buddhist studies, earning degrees at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Edinburgh. He held positions at Vikramashila Pirivena, Sarnath, SOAS, Toronto, and served as head of the London Buddhist Vihara (~1957–1990).

Han de Wit is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Amsterdam under Adriaan de Groot and with Chögyam Trungpa, and later held a post at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam.
Hank Glassman works in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He has served as a faculty member at Haverford College (attested 2009, 2019).

Hanna Havnevik specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She has held posts as professor (attested 2006–2008) and professor emerita (attested 2026) at the University of Oslo.

Hanns Oertel was an Indologist and linguist who completed his doctorate at Yale University under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Yale (1891–1917), Harvard (1903–1904), Basel (1920), Marburg (1922), and held a chair at the University of Munich (1925–1935).

Hanns-Peter Schmidt worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Ludwig Alsdorf at the University of Hamburg (PhD ~1957). He taught at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University, Tübingen, and UCLA (professor, 1965–2000).

Hans Delbrück was a historian who studied at the University of Bonn (~1869–1873). He held academic posts at Frederick William University Berlin in 1885 and the Humboldt University of Berlin (~1881–1921).

Hans Harder is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Hamburg, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg, completing his doctorate under Rahul Peter Das (~1997) and habilitation (~2006). He held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (1995–2007) and Heidelberg (2007).

Hans Hartog is an Indologist who studied at Tübingen, Kirchliche Hochschule Wuppertal/Bethel, Munich, and Marburg. He completed his PhD under Friedrich Heiler at Marburg in 1939, having also studied under Hanns Oertel, Walther Wüst, and others.

Hans Heinrich Schaeder was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Leipzig (~1930–1931), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1931–1945), and the University of Göttingen (~1946–1957).

Hans Henrich Hock is a linguist and Indologist who completed graduate studies at Northwestern University and Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill. He held a post as Professor of Linguistics and Sanskrit at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign from ~1967.
Hans Krahe was a linguist who held academic appointments at the University of Würzburg (~1936–1946), Heidelberg University (~1946–1949), and the University of Tübingen (~1949–1965).
